name: AI Use Case Assessment
description: Turn any AI/agentic use case idea (chat, uploaded doc, or attached file) into an evidence-grounded, rubric-scored assessment with a customer-branded HTML report. Guides the user question-by-question through intake, categorisation, strengthening, scoring, and reporting — grounded in the Agentic Use Case Assessment Rubric v2. Runs in Microsoft Scout and Microsoft 365 Copilot Cowork.
author: Alicja Gilderdale
coverImageAlt: A level precision balance weighs a populated impact group against an equally populated practical-complexity group above blank evidence cards.
coverImagePrompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: AI.Tedt.org skill gallery cover
Primary request: Create a premium editorial illustration of an early AI use-case idea being assessed by visibly balancing two equally important, fully populated factors: beneficial impact and practical complexity.
Scene/backdrop: A quiet warm-paper evaluation table within a deep slate studio, surrounded by generous negative space and a clean uninterrupted margin on every side.
Subject: One centered precision two-pan balance with a perfectly level beam. The left pan is fully populated by a luminous cyan outcome prism, one restrained orange benefit sphere, and three small warm-paper value tokens, together representing impact. The right pan is equally populated and has the same perceived visual weight, holding a compact cluster of interlocking navy and cyan dependency blocks, two linked rings, and three small warm-paper effort tokens, together representing practical complexity. Both pans must clearly contain their full object groups; neither pan may be empty or visually secondary. A small ordered stack of blank evidence cards sits beneath the center pivot and feeds the assessment mechanism.
Style/medium: Premium editorial illustration with tactile dimensional detail, matte ceramic forms, translucent acrylic, fine dark metal, and restrained paper texture.
Composition/framing: Exact 16:10 landscape. Keep the complete balance, both populated pans, every object group, and the full evidence-card stack inside the central 76% of the canvas, leaving at least 8% empty margin on the left, right, top, and bottom. Every essential subject must stay fully inside the central 84% safe area, from 8% to 92% of both width and height. Nothing may touch or cross the frame. Use a strong centered symmetrical silhouette with two equally prominent populated factors, legible at small card size.
Lighting/mood: Calm, capable, evidence-minded, quietly technical; focused cyan rim light with one restrained orange calibration accent.
Color palette: Warm paper #F8F6F0, slate #101820, navy #00446F, cyan #00A9E0, sparing orange #E86027.
Constraints: No text, letters, numbers, quotations, interface labels, scale markings, icons, logos, trademarks, or watermark; no pseudo-writing or writing-like lines; no paw imagery or paw logo; no cats or cat silhouettes; no brain, robot, humanoid, product UI, Microsoft Fluent gradients, or Microsoft branding. Do not leave either pan empty. Do not crop or clip the balance, pans, objects, cards, or supports.
Targeted correction of the attached draft: Preserve the exact centered level balance, the two equally prominent populated pans, all large impact and complexity objects, evidence-card stack, lighting, materials, and crop-safe placement. Remove every etched or embossed mark, pictogram, bar, dot pattern, ring pattern, or symbol from the six small warm-paper tokens in both pans, leaving those tokens as completely plain matte geometric forms. Do not change the populated visual weight of either pan and do not introduce any new mark, icon, text, logo, paw, cat, product UI, or branding.
